gram-heatmap: Twelve points on a line and their Gram matrix \(K_{ij}=k(x_i,x_j)\) for a Gaussian kernel at bandwidth \(1\). A kernel is positive definite exactly when this matrix is positive semidefinite for every sample; narrowing the bandwidth drives it toward the identity.
kernel-lab: Kernel ridge regression on six points with a Gaussian kernel (bandwidth \(1\), ridge \(\lambda=10^{-2}\)). The curve is the exact solution \(f=\sum_i\alpha_i k(\cdot,x_i)\) with \(\alpha=(K+\lambda n I)^{-1}y\).
feature-lift: Two classes that no line separates in the plane become linearly separable under the lift \(\phi(x)=(x_1,x_2,x_1^2+x_2^2)\): a flat plane slices the inner ring off cleanly. The polynomial kernel computes \(\langle\phi(x),\phi(x')\rangle\) without ever building the third coordinate.
svm-margin: The maximum-margin decision boundary (solid) and its \(\pm1\) margins for two classes under a Gaussian kernel. Circled points are the support vectors, the only ones with \(\alpha_i>0\).
mmd-twosample: Samples from two distributions \(P\) and \(Q\) and their maximum mean discrepancy \(\mathrm{MMD}^2=\mathbb E\,k(X,X')+\mathbb E\,k(Y,Y')-2\,\mathbb E\,k(X,Y)\), the RKHS distance between their kernel mean embeddings. With a characteristic kernel it vanishes only when \(P=Q\).
rff-converge: The Gaussian kernel \(k(x,x')=e^{-(x-x')^2/2}\) (dark curve) against its \(D=20\) random Fourier feature estimate \(\hat k=\tfrac1D\sum_j\cos(w_jx+b_j)\cos(w_jx'+b_j)\), as a function of the gap \(x-x'\). Bochner's theorem makes the true kernel the average of these random features.
bo-loop: A Bayesian optimization loop on a hidden objective: the shaded band is the Gaussian-process posterior \(\mu\pm2\sigma\) refit after each query, and the lower strip is the acquisition function whose argmax (dashed line) chooses the next point.
cme-explore: The conditional mean embedding \(\beta(x^*)=(K_X+n\lambda I)^{-1}k_X(x^*)\) applied to sixty samples: the side profile is the embedded conditional \(\sum_i\beta_i\,l(\cdot,y_i)\) and the dot marks its conditional mean at the conditioning point \(x^*\).
heat-graph: Node colors are the graph heat kernel \(r(i,j)\) built from the eigenpairs of the Laplacian, for a fixed source node. A small diffusion time keeps similarity inside the source's cluster; a larger time spreads it across the bridge.
spectrum-surgery: The exact spectrum of a \(\tanh\) similarity matrix on ten points; the negative (Kreĭn) eigenvalues are drawn in red. Of the three PSD repairs, clipping the negative eigenvalues to zero changes the matrix least in Frobenius norm — the nearest-PSD solution.
svgd-flow: Stein variational gradient descent transports particles toward the two-mode target \(p=\tfrac12\mathcal N(-2,0.6^2)+\tfrac12\mathcal N(2,0.8^2)\). Kernel repulsion spreads the swarm across the low-density valley so both modes are populated; the empirical kernel Stein discrepancy falls as the flow converges.
sinkhorn-plan: The entropic optimal-transport plan \(\pi=\operatorname{diag}(u)\,K\,\operatorname{diag}(v)\) between a two-bump source and a wide target, converged by alternating Sinkhorn normalizations \(u\leftarrow a\oslash(Kv)\), \(v\leftarrow b\oslash(K^\top u)\).
herding-greedy: Kernel herding greedily places nodes at the argmax of the herding criterion for a standard-normal target (Gaussian kernel, closed-form embedding \(\mu_P(x)=e^{-x^2/4}/\sqrt2\)). The lower panel shows the worst-case integration error falling as nodes accrue, faster still when the nodes are optimally reweighted.
sig-draw: The depth-2 path signature of a stroke: level 1 is the displacement, and the genuinely new level-2 coordinate is the Lévy area \(\tfrac12(S^{12}-S^{21})\), the signed area (shaded) between the path and its chord. The signature depends only on the trace, not its parametrization.
dp-fill: The dynamic-programming table for the gap-weighted subsequence kernel on the words *cat* and *car* (\(\lambda=0.5\), \(p=2\)): each cell combines its neighbors with the stated \(\lambda\) weights, giving \(K_2=\lambda^4=0.0625\) and normalized similarity \(0.4444\).
permutation-null: The permutation null distribution of the kernel two-sample statistic, built by repeatedly relabeling the pooled samples. The observed statistic (line) against the \(\alpha=0.05\) critical quantile gives the test's p-value.
wl-refine: Weisfeiler–Lehman color refinement: at each round every node is relabeled by the multiset of its neighbors' colors, so structurally distinct nodes split into new classes. These refined colors are the features of the WL graph kernel.
conformal-coverage: Under a misspecified Gaussian process the native predictive interval under-covers, while a split-conformal wrapper restores the nominal 90% coverage with a finite-sample, distribution-free guarantee.
influence-glow: Every kernel-ridge prediction is a signed sum over training points; the closed-form leave-one-out and influence match brute-force refits to machine precision, so attribution is exact and free.
drift-mmd: MMD drift monitoring: the kernel two-sample statistic between a reference window and a live window, tested against its permutation null, flags a shifted deployment distribution (small p) while a matched window does not.
active-variance: Uncertainty-driven active learning queries where the Gaussian-process posterior variance is largest; the variance-guided design reaches a target accuracy in far fewer labels than random sampling.
quasiperiodic-gp: A quasi-periodic Gaussian process (a periodic kernel times an RBF decay) fits a noisy stellar light curve and recovers the rotation period with a calibrated interval.
matched-filter: Matched filtering as a noise-weighted inner product: correlating a template against noisy data peaks sharply at the true lag, the optimal linear detector for a known signal in coloured noise.
onthefly-mlip: An on-the-fly machine-learned interatomic potential: a Gaussian process fits the energy curve and triggers a reference (DFT) call wherever its posterior variance exceeds a threshold, recovering the equilibrium bond length from few evaluations.
